messages:
jon: Seeing 2-5% packet loss and RDMA timeouts between GPU pods after today's Cilium canary (1.23.4) with encap-hybrid enabled. Affected nodepool: us-west2-gpu-canary. Anyone else seeing this?
ashley: Is this only the west2 canary? rollback or mitigate? :thinking_face:
jon: Confirmed only west2 canary so far. Training pods show `rdma` timeouts and nv_peer_mem errors. Minimal logs: 
```
[rdma] ib_event: port 1 fatal err
nv_peer_mem: failed to map page: -22
```

lee: Could be MTU/path frag. What do `ip link`/`ip -s link` show on those nodes?
maria: Also: we run a mixed Cilium+Calico setup in some clusters — encap changes can add headers and push RDMA packets into fragmentation territory.
jon: Quick node dump: `eth0 mtu 1500`, `cni0 mtu 1450`, calico ipip interface shows 1440. `/proc/net/ipv4/ipfrag_*` counters climbing.
lee: That smells like encap header making large RDMA frames exceed MTU -> fragmentation or drop. Is GSO/GRO being handled end-to-end?
jon: `ethtool -k eth0` shows GSO on. But dmesg on GPU node shows repeated peer-mem failures.
maria: Reproduction idea: RDMA pingpong + iperf with large segment length to trigger frag. Also check sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh.
jon: sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh=262144. iperf3 with `-l 64k` shows bursty drops between pods on different nodes in the pool.
ashley: Short-term mitigation: disable encap-hybrid on canary nodes and rollback the cilium canary. @infra-bot can you start a rollback on west2-gpu-canary?
infra-bot: Rolling back cilium-release/1.23.4 -> 1.22.9 on nodepool west2-gpu-canary. Started at 2012345690. ETA ~3m. :gear:
sre: Good plan. We should avoid changing MTU globally for now — too risky for prod. Rollback + capture packets during rollback, then run controlled RDMA tests.
jon: Repro steps for post-rollback validation: 1) schedule two gpu pods on different nodes in canary pool; 2) run `iperf3 -c <peer> -l 64k -b 0`; 3) run RDMA pingpong test from mlx driver.
maria: After rollback, gather tcpdump on veth/cni interfaces and rdma kernel logs, then open an incident with label `CNI-encap-frag` and attach captures.
jon: Rollback finished, tests green. RDMA pingpong succeeded, iperf no packet loss. Will upload packet captures and follow up with a minimal repro and kernel+encap headers for root cause analysis. :white_check_mark:
